Package paint.shared.utils

Class PaintLogger

java.lang.Object
paint.shared.utils.PaintLogger
public final class PaintLogger extends Object
Static logger class for color-coded console and file logging.

Supports multiple severity levels, formatted messages, and persistent log storage under a project’s "Logs" directory.

    • setLevel

      public static void setLevel(String level)
      Sets the log level using a string value. Accepts: "DEBUG", "INFO", "WARN", "WARNING", "ERROR". Defaults to INFO for unknown or null input.
      Parameters:
      level - textual level name

    • getLevelName

      public static String getLevelName()
      Returns the current log level as an uppercase string.
      Returns:
      the name of the current log level (e.g., "DEBUG", "INFO").

    • initialise

      public static void initialise(Path projectPath, String logBaseName)
      Initializes the logger by creating a "Logs" directory and a new numbered log file. Logs are written to both file and GUI console.
      Parameters:
      projectPath - base directory under which the "Logs" folder will be created
      logBaseName - base name used for the log file

    • close

      public static void close()
      Flushes and closes the current log file. Later messages still go to the console output, but not to a file, until initialise(Path, String) is called again.

      An open file cannot be deleted on Windows, so a log file must be closed before its folder can be removed (for example a test's temporary directory).

    • error

      public static void error(String message, Throwable t)
      Logs an ERROR message together with the full stack trace of a throwable. Prefer this over printStackTrace() / System.err so the diagnostic reaches the log file and console like any other message.
      Parameters:
      message - descriptive context for the error
      t - the throwable whose stack trace should be logged (may be null)

    • raw

      public static void raw(String text)
      Prints text directly to console without timestamps or level formatting. Useful for inline output such as progress bars.
      Parameters:
